title: Rule allows any source to reach any destination on any port
description: Policy 3 "WAN-Full-Access" allows any source to reach any destination on any service, for traffic coming in from the internet.

title: Firmware has a vulnerability that attackers are known to use
description: FortiOS 7.2.5 is affected by CVE-2024-21762 (FG-IR-24-015): an out-of-bounds write in the SSL-VPN daemon that lets an unauthenticated attacker run code on the firewall. The vulnerable code is in SSL-VPN, which is enabled on wan1 here and reachable from the internet. It's in CISA's catalog of known exploited vulnerabilities.

title: Firewall management is reachable from the internet
description: Interface wan1 faces the internet (it has role wan) and accepts HTTPS, HTTP, SSH and telnet management connections from any address.
impact: The admin login page, SSH or SNMP is open on an internet-facing interface. FortiOS has had several authentication bypass bugs in the admin interface, and exposed management is scanned constantly.
recommendation: Remove https, http, ssh, telnet and snmp from allowaccess on internet-facing interfaces. If you have to manage over the internet, limit sources with a local-in policy or use a VPN.

title: Rule never takes effect because an earlier rule does the opposite
description: Policy 5 "Deny-Partner-SSH-shadowed" (deny) sits below policy 4 "Allow-Partner-SSH" (accept), and policy 4 already matches every packet policy 5 would. FortiGate uses the first match, so policy 5 never takes effect and the traffic it's meant to block is allowed.
impact: FortiGate stops at the first matching rule. An earlier rule with the opposite action catches all of this rule's traffic, so a block here doesn't block anything, or an allow here never allows anything.
recommendation: Move this rule above the broader one, or narrow the broader rule so it no longer covers this traffic.
compliance: CIS: 4.1; NIST CSF: PR.AC-5; MITRE ATT&CK: T1562; PCI DSS: 1.2.1; ISO 27001: A.8.20, A.8.9

title: Admin accounts that can log in from anywhere

impact: Without trusted hosts, anyone who can reach the admin interface can try these accounts' passwords.
recommendation: Set trusthost entries to your management networks. Trusted hosts only help if every admin account has them, and they don't stop attacks that happen before login, so also restrict the admin interfaces with a local-in policy.

recommendation: Remove telnet and http from allowaccess on every interface and use SSH and HTTPS only.

title: Scanners can't see inside encrypted traffic
description: Policy 4 "Allow-Partner-SSH" relies on IPS and antivirus, but its SSL profile (cert-inspect) only does certificate inspection. Encrypted content passes these scanners unseen.
impact: Antivirus, DLP, file filtering and email filtering need decrypted content. With certificate inspection or no inspection they only see the handshake, so most modern traffic goes unscanned.
recommendation: Use a deep-inspection SSL/SSH profile on rules where you rely on these scanners, with exemptions for sensitive categories such as banking and health.

recommendation: Set intrazone deny and write rules for the traffic that should flow, or split unrelated networks into separate zones.
